notes: Muse's sibling to claudecode's already-observed background-subagent cell, exercising the SAME adapter-agnostic held-working mechanism (session_detector_subagent.go's hasActiveChildren/reevaluateParent) via muse's own subagent_spawn (admission-only, async by construction -- no blocking parameter exists) followed deliberately by NO subagent_read_result before the parent's own reply ends. Single-birth adapter (session id = session directory basename), so birth is anchored to start UNPINNED. The scenario's user-observable claim has no separate state for 'parent's own reply landed but is held' -- it is the SAME continuous working span that both the parent's own turn AND the background child's lifetime ride on -- so the arc is asserted as one long held_working span (min_delay_ms past when a normal tool-calling turn would have gone ready on its own, duration_at_least_ms covering the child's plausible runtime) followed by a single terminal drained_ready phase once the background child finishes. Deliberately does NOT phase-assert the child's own session as a discrete new_session-pinned phase: muse's memory-reminder micro-agents (goal-reminder/verify-reminder, format-spec §9) are ALSO ParentSessionID-linked via the identical nested subagent/<id>/ path and could otherwise be vacuously matched as 'the' background child by an unpinned new_session phase (the exact contamination risk the 4-1 multiple-sessions-same-cwd cell's notes document for this corpus) -- the parent-only arc is both the scenario's actual point and the safe thing to assert. Cost: no dollar cost is ever persisted in muse's transcript (strict key scan, format-spec §6) and no muse model has a pricing entry in core/pkg/capacity yet, so cost_nonzero=false -- a caveat, not a bug. Model pinned muse-spark-1.3-contributor, confirmed live across every already-recorded muse cell on this machine (basic-turn, token-accounting, multiple-sessions-same-cwd).
